CONFIG.EVENT_TAGLINE: Debug it. Rebuild it. Buzz for it.
CONFIG.COLLEGE_AFFILIATION: Approved by AICTE, New Delhi. Affiliated to Anna University, Chennai.
CONFIG.COLLEGE_ACCREDITATION: ISO 9001:2008 Certified Institution & Accredited by NBA
CONFIG.COLLEGE_ADDRESS: Kalasalingam Nagar, IT Corridor, Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), Kazhipattur, Chennai – 603103, Tamil Nadu
CONFIG.VENUE: Anand Institute of Higher Technology, OMR, Kazhipattur, Chennai – 603103

GENERAL_RULES: A laptop is optional. Teams may use the lab computer provided, and each team competes on one device only.
The event consists of three levels, gradually increasing in difficulty: Bug Bounty, Sight Unseen and Buzz or Bust.
Participants compete in teams of 1 to 4 members. Registration is spot registration only, at the venue.
Mobile phones are strictly prohibited as a second device in every level.
Discussion is allowed only within your own team. Talking to or helping other teams is not allowed.
The decision of the event coordinators and judges will be final.

LEVELS.name: Bug Bounty
LEVELS.tagline: Ten broken programs. Ten minutes. Five languages.
LEVELS.qualifier: Top 5 teams from each lab advance
rules: Teams will be given 10 broken programs to fix within 10 minutes. The programs cover:
Easy, Medium and Hard difficulty levels.
C, C++, Java, Python and JavaScript.
Each program must be fixed in the language it is written in.
The round runs in Lab 1 and Lab 2 at the same time, with 10 teams in each lab.
The top 5 teams from each lab will qualify for the next level.

scoring.label: Points
scoring.text: Each solved question earns 100 points, dropping by 10 every minute, down to a minimum of 10.

scoring.label: Difficulty
scoring.text: All questions carry the same points. Wrong submissions cost nothing.

LEVELS.name: Sight Unseen
LEVELS.tagline: Watch a website once. Rebuild it from memory.
rules: A live website will be shown on the projector only once, for 5 minutes.
Teams may take written notes, but photos or recordings of the website are not allowed.
Teams then get 35 minutes to rebuild the website from memory using an AI tool.
AI tools and internet access are allowed in this level.
The top 5 teams will advance to the final level.

scoring.label: Scale
scoring.text: Each category is scored from 0 to 10, for a maximum of 50.

scoring.label: Layout, Colors, Animations, Contents
scoring.text: How closely the rebuild matches the original website.

scoring.label: Prompt
scoring.text: Fewer and clearer prompts score higher.

LEVELS.name: Buzz or Bust
LEVELS.tagline: Buzz first, code offline, or lose the points anyway.
rules: Every team starts with 100 points, and scores carry across all 5 questions.
Each question shows an expected output or a problem to build.
The first three teams to press the buzzer get to code. The other two sit out that question.
The three teams get 10 minutes to code offline, using only a notepad or offline editor, and must run their code to show the output.
The top three teams with the highest total score will be declared winners.

scoring.label: Output
scoring.text: Judges rank the three attempts by correctness. 1st gets 20 points back, 2nd gets 15, 3rd gets 10.

REGULATIONS: Teams must complete each level within the given time limit.
In Bug Bounty, every fix must genuinely work. It is re-tested with hidden data, so printing the answer will be rejected.
A solved question locks in, and its points cannot be lost.
A team must solve at least one question in Bug Bounty to qualify.
Keep your Team ID safe. It is needed to rejoin if your device disconnects.
Tampering with lab equipment, the network or the buzzer system will lead to disqualification from the entire event.
CODE_OF_CONDUCT: Respect event coordinators, fellow participants, and judges.
Fair play is mandatory; copying, sharing answers or any unethical behaviour will lead to disqualification.
No internet, AI tools or outside help in Bug Bounty and Buzz or Bust.
WINNING: The top three teams with the highest cumulative scores in Buzz or Bust will be declared winners.
In case of a tie, the event coordinators and judges will decide the final standing.

PROGRESSION.detail: 10 teams in Lab 1, 10 teams in Lab 2

FAQ.q: How do I register for Stack and Level?
FAQ.a: Registration is spot registration only, at the venue. You can also pre-register through the Technofest 2026 form so we know you are coming — but the team you compete with is confirmed at the venue on the day.

FAQ.q: How many people can be in a team?
FAQ.a: Participants compete in teams of 1 to 4 members. You can enter alone or with up to three teammates.

FAQ.q: Do I need to bring a laptop?
FAQ.a: A laptop is optional. Teams may use the lab computer provided, and each team competes on one device only.

FAQ.q: Can I use my phone during the event?
FAQ.a: No. Mobile phones are strictly prohibited as a second device in every level.

FAQ.q: Are AI tools and the internet allowed?
FAQ.a: Only in Sight Unseen, where AI tools and internet access are allowed. There is no internet, AI tools or outside help in Bug Bounty and Buzz or Bust.

FAQ.q: How do teams qualify for the next level?
FAQ.a: In Bug Bounty the top 5 teams from each lab qualify, and a team must solve at least one question to qualify at all. In Sight Unseen the top 5 teams advance to the final level.

FAQ.q: What happens if my device disconnects?
FAQ.a: Keep your Team ID safe — it is needed to rejoin if your device disconnects.

FAQ.q: Which languages do the Bug Bounty programs use?
FAQ.a: The 10 broken programs cover C, C++, Java, Python and JavaScript, across Easy, Medium and Hard difficulty levels. Each program must be fixed in the language it is written in.
The top three teams with the highest cumulative scores in Buzz or Bust will be declared winners. In case of a tie, the event coordinators and judges will decide the final standing.
First prize is ₹1,500, second prize is ₹1,000 and third prize is ₹750 — each awarded with a certificate.
